area: Image analysis (Module F, src/modules/images.py) and advanced image forensics (Module H, src/modules/forensics.py) — embedded-image checks, screenshot/scan detection, paste-artifact noise analysis, Error Level Analysis (ELA), and disabled clone detection. Both modules are wired into src/analyzer.py (lines 141, 149) with scoring weights images=0.8, forensics=0.9 (src/scoring.py:30-31).

checks.name: IMAGES_SCREENSHOT_DETECTED (check_screenshot_dimensions)
checks.description: images.py:159-193. Compares each embedded image's pixel dimensions against 10 hardcoded desktop/laptop screen resolutions (images.py:139-150), both orientations, ±20px tolerance (images.py:156). Severity HIGH (30 points) per image.
checks.quality: Cheap but brittle: desktop-only list (no phone resolutions, no 1600x900/2560x1600/ultrawide), exact-match so cropped/resized screenshots never match, HIGH severity is harsh for a signal with common legitimate causes. Tolerance was sensibly tightened from 50 to 20px after a documented A4-at-90PPI false positive (images.py:152-155).

checks.name: IMAGES_RESOLUTION_MISMATCH (check_resolution_consistency)
checks.description: images.py:196-242. Computes pseudo-DPI per image as pixel_width / (page_width/72) — assumes every image spans the full page (images.py:113-115). Flags MEDIUM if max_dpi > 4x min_dpi and min_dpi > 10.
checks.quality: Fundamentally broken: DPI is derived from PAGE size, not the image's placed rectangle, so it effectively compares raw pixel counts; a 300px logo in a 1-inch box computes as ~36 DPI. Fires or stays silent at random relative to its stated purpose. Needs page.get_image_rects(xref). The comment at images.py:111-112 admits the shortcut.

checks.name: IMAGES_HEAVY_COMPRESSION (check_heavy_compression)
checks.description: images.py:245-287. For DCT/JPEG-filtered images, compression_ratio = width*height*3 / stored_bytes; flags MEDIUM if ratio > 80:1 (images.py:274).
checks.quality: Naive: hardcodes 3 bytes/pixel so grayscale JPEG scans get a 3x-inflated ratio (real 27:1 flags as 80:1); flat graphics and text scans legitimately exceed 80:1 while a q-60 double-saved photo can stay under. JPX ignored. Should read JPEG quantization tables to estimate quality instead of using size.

checks.name: IMAGES_EXCESSIVE_COUNT (check_image_count)
checks.description: images.py:290-328. Flags MEDIUM if images-per-page > 15. Contains a dead loop (images.py:321-326) identifying full-page images that just does `pass` with a TODO.
checks.quality: Arbitrary threshold, mostly harmless. get_images(full=True) counts repeated logo xrefs once per page and counts resource-listed-but-never-drawn images, inflating counts. Dead TODO loop is superseded by check_image_only_pdf and should be deleted.

checks.name: IMAGES_NO_IMAGES (check_no_images)
checks.description: images.py:331-358. Flags LOW (5 points) if zero raster images and text_length > 500 ('unusual for branded invoices').
checks.quality: Weak premise: vector logos (InDesign/Illustrator/LaTeX, most utility-company PDFs) are invisible to page.get_images(), so professionally branded documents get flagged for having no images. Systematic noise pointing the wrong way — a text-only digital PDF is if anything a positive trust signal.

checks.name: IMAGES_IMAGE_ONLY_PDF / IMAGES_MOSTLY_IMAGE_PDF (check_image_only_pdf)
checks.description: images.py:365-444. Counts 'full-page' images (width>500 AND height>700 px regardless of placement). If count >= 0.8*page_count: chars_per_page < 50 → MEDIUM IMAGE_ONLY; < 200 → MEDIUM MOSTLY_IMAGE.
checks.quality: Right concept, loose implementation: pixel thresholds ignore placement (large product photo counts as full-page; low-res fax scan doesn't); aggregate count doesn't require images on distinct pages (8 photos on one page of a 10-page doc triggers); and if the OCR fallback has populated text_by_page, chars_per_page exceeds 200 and true image-only scans are never flagged.

checks.name: IMAGES_PASTE_NOISE_ANOMALY (check_paste_artifacts + find_amount_regions)
checks.description: images.py:456-655. Regex-locates text blocks containing currency amounts (AMOUNT_PATTERN, images.py:456-460), renders pages at zoom 2, computes noise = gray - GaussianBlur(5x5), skips pages with total noise variance < 1.0 (assumed digital), flags HIGH if an amount region's noise variance < 1/4 of the surrounding neighborhood variance (padding = 1x region size, neighborhood var must exceed 2.0).
checks.quality: The most targeted check and the right fraud scenario, but the physics is off: the Gaussian residual is dominated by text-edge energy, not sensor noise. So (a) the <1.0 digital-page gate almost never triggers (antialiased text alone exceeds it) — the claimed digital-PDF exclusion is false; (b) a pasted region containing typed text has high edge energy → high variance → never flagged; (c) variance ratios mostly measure text density. Also the neighborhood window INCLUDES the region itself (images.py:619-624), biasing the comparison, and region bboxes are whole text blocks that can span a full table row. Credit: white-level analysis was tested and honestly removed (images.py:647-652).

checks.name: FORENSICS_ELA_MAJOR_EDIT / FORENSICS_ELA_MINOR_EDIT (compute_ela / detect_suspicious_regions / analyze_ela)
checks.description: forensics.py:63-170, 411-454. For each embedded image >= 200x200 px: re-encode JPEG q=95, amplify absdiff x20, threshold grayscale ELA at mean+3σ, keep contours >= 500 px area. Total suspicious area > 3% of image → MEDIUM (-15); > 5% → HIGH (-30). Runs on every decodable image regardless of original format.
checks.quality: Textbook ELA neutered by three flaws: (1) never checks base_image['ext'], so PNG/Flate/CCITT-converted images with no JPEG history get meaningless ELA; (2) cv2.multiply(diff, 20) saturates at 255 (forensics.py:95) — any diff >= 13 flattens to 255, destroying the relative-brightness signal and potentially pushing mean+3σ above 255 (empty mask); (3) the 3%/5% area gates require an edit covering a huge fraction of the image, while the module's own stated scenario (edit one amount) covers ~0.05-0.1% of a 300dpi scan — orders of magnitude below threshold.

checks.name: Clone / copy-move detection (detect_clones / analyze_clones) — DISABLED dead code
checks.description: forensics.py:177-318. Grid-aligned 16px blocks, perceptual hash (8x8 mean-brightness bins, 16 levels), verification via MAD < 3, Manhattan distance >= 64, >= 10 verified blocks required, images > 2MP skipped, groups on <= 2 rows or <= 2 columns discarded as tables. Integration commented out at forensics.py:458-462 due to table false positives.
checks.quality: Dead code. Even re-enabled it cannot catch the target fraud: a copied digit spans 1-2 grid blocks (10 required), non-overlapping grid alignment misses arbitrary-offset pastes, the <=2-rows/cols filter discards small matches, and the 2MP cap excludes a standard 300dpi A4 scan (~8.7MP). Needs redesign (overlapping blocks or keypoint matching + offset-vector consistency), not re-tuning.

weaknesses: images.py:113-115 — DPI is computed as image_pixels / page_size_inches, assuming every image covers the full page. This is wrong for any placed image (logo, signature, stamp) and makes check_resolution_consistency (images.py:196-242) compare pixel counts, not resolutions. Fix: page.get_image_rects(xref) for the placed rect.

forensics.py:95 — cv2.multiply(diff, 20) saturates uint8 at 255; all diffs >= 13 become identical, flattening the ELA signal that detect_suspicious_regions then thresholds. With high mean the mean+3σ threshold can exceed 255, producing an empty mask (silent no-detection). Amplification should happen in float, or thresholding should be done on the raw diff.

forensics.py:354-365 — ELA runs on whatever doc.extract_image returns without checking base_image['ext']. PNG/Flate images and CCITT/JBIG2 scans (which PyMuPDF converts to PNG) have no JPEG compression history, so ELA output is noise. SMask (soft mask) xrefs >= 200x200 are also analyzed as if they were photos.

forensics.py:47-48 — ELA_SUSPICIOUS_RATIO (3%) and ELA_HIGHLY_SUSPICIOUS_RATIO (5%) gate on total suspicious area as a fraction of the whole image. A single edited amount on an A4 300dpi scan is ~0.05-0.1% of the image; the module's own headline fraud scenario can never reach its flag threshold. Detection statistics should be local/windowed, not global.

images.py:589-593 — the page_noise < 1.0 'purely digital PDF' gate does not work: the Gaussian-blur residual is dominated by antialiased text-edge energy, so virtually every rendered text page passes the gate. The docstring's claim that digital PDFs are excluded (images.py:534-538) is false in practice, causing both wasted compute and digital-PDF false positives.

images.py:615-624 — the 'neighborhood' window used for noise comparison includes the amount region itself, biasing neighborhood_var toward region_var and weakening the ratio test; region bboxes are whole text blocks (find_amount_regions, images.py:491-507), which for tables can span the entire row, diluting any local anomaly.

images.py:456-460 — AMOUNT_PATTERN misses amounts without two decimals ('1 000 €', '1000 EUR', '25€'), does not handle US comma-thousands except via a partial match, and the bare second alternative matches ANY d.dd decimal (quantities, rates, version numbers), so 'amount regions' are both over- and under-inclusive. Fraudulent edits to dates, IBANs, names, or addresses are never examined at all.

forensics.py:56 + 241 — CLONE_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = 2,000,000 skips clone detection for any image over 2MP; a standard 300dpi A4 scan is ~8.7MP, so the check (were it enabled) would skip exactly the documents it targets.

forensics.py:458-462 — clone detection is entirely disabled (commented-out integration); ~140 lines (forensics.py:177-318) are dead code, and forensics.py:409/419's suspicious_images counter is incremented but never used.
images.py:321-326 — dead loop in check_image_count that identifies full-page images and does `pass` with a TODO; superseded by check_image_only_pdf.

images.py:701-704 and forensics.py:455-456 — broad `except Exception` swallows paste-detection and per-image ELA failures with only a log warning; the module still reports its normal score and confidence, so a systematically failing check silently looks like a clean result. find_amount_regions (images.py:488-489) likewise returns [] on any get_text error.

images.py:130, forensics.py:377 — doc.close() is not in try/finally; an exception mid-loop leaks the document handle. Also images.py:104-108 silently maps extraction failure to size_bytes=0, which then silently disables the compression check for that image (images.py:265).

Module docstring promises 'Image placement - Images placed over text (covering content)' (images.py:11) and CLAUDE.md lists it, but no such check exists anywhere — the white-rectangle-over-original-amount attack via PDF drawing operators is completely unhandled.
images.py:270 — uncompressed size hardcodes 3 channels and ignores bpc/colorspace: grayscale JPEGs get 3x-overestimated compression ratios, CMYK underestimated.

images.py:93 + counting — page.get_images(full=True) lists resource-referenced images even if never drawn, and the same xref repeated on N pages counts N times; no dedup by xref, inflating IMAGES_EXCESSIVE_COUNT and skewing resolution stats.

images.py:569-575 — pixmap conversion assumes n==3 means RGB; if a pixmap ever carries 4 channels (alpha/CMYK edge cases), cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR on a 4-channel array raises, which the outer try in analyze_images then swallows for the whole paste check.
images.py:662-667 — SEVERITY_POINTS is a local duplicate of the scoring table in scoring.py (as is the inline -30/-15 logic in forensics.py:464-470); divergence risk if the org-wide weights change.

Performance/architecture: the PDF is opened and images re-extracted at least three separate times (images.py:83, images.py:549, forensics.py:341) plus the main extractor pass; page rendering at zoom 2 is repeated per module. One shared extraction pass should feed both modules.
forensics.py:474 — confidence = min(0.9, 0.5 + 0.1*n_images) rewards image COUNT, not analysis success; ten tiny decorative images yield 0.9 confidence even if every ELA call threw.
false_positive_risks: Honest paper invoice scanned by the customer (flatbed or scan app, JPEG at typical scanner quality): stacks IMAGES_IMAGE_ONLY_PDF (medium), often IMAGES_HEAVY_COMPRESSION (medium — text scans compress far beyond 80:1), and FORENSICS_ELA_MAJOR_EDIT (high — dense text edges produce strong ELA response easily exceeding 3-5% of image area on a never-JPEG or heavily-saturated ELA map). A perfectly legitimate scan can lose 60+ points from these two modules alone.

Grayscale scanned documents specifically: the 3-bytes/pixel assumption (images.py:270) triples the computed compression ratio, so a normal-quality grayscale scan flags IMAGES_HEAVY_COMPRESSION at an effective real ratio of ~27:1.

Digital invoice containing a noisy photographic element near the totals (product photo, scanned signature, stamp, embedded ID photo): the paste-noise check compares the clean digital amount text (near-zero residual variance) against a neighborhood window inflated by the adjacent photo's noise → HIGH IMAGES_PASTE_NOISE_ANOMALY on an untouched document, precisely because the digital-PDF gate (page_noise < 1.0) fails to exclude it.

Legitimate personal-workflow screenshots: bank/mobile-app payment confirmations or e-tickets exported by screenshotting at exactly 1920x1080/1366x768 etc. get a HIGH severity IMAGES_SCREENSHOT_DETECTED (30 points) — a very common non-fraud behavior for individuals submitting proofs.

Professionally produced text-only or vector-branded PDFs (LaTeX invoices, accounting-software output, utility bills with vector logos): flagged IMAGES_NO_IMAGES because vector artwork is invisible to page.get_images() — the most trustworthy class of document receives a penalty for its trustworthy trait.

Expense reports / real-estate diagnostic reports / illustrated statements with many small receipt photos or per-line icons: IMAGES_EXCESSIVE_COUNT at >15 images/page, and repeated per-page letterhead images inflate the count further because xrefs are counted once per page.
Documents mixing a high-res full-page scan appendix with small UI icons: the pseudo-DPI spread (really just pixel-count spread) exceeds 4x → IMAGES_RESOLUTION_MISMATCH on a normal composite document.

Photographed (not scanned) documents re-saved once by a phone scan app: uniform JPEG artifacts plus paper texture push large contiguous areas over the mean+3σ ELA threshold; with the x20 saturated amplification the ELA map becomes near-binary and contour areas balloon past the 3-5% gates.
false_negative_gaps: The flagship scenario — a single amount changed in Paint/Photoshop on a scanned invoice — is missed by ELA because a ~100x30px edit is ~0.05-0.1% of a 300dpi A4 scan, far below the 3% ELA_SUSPICIOUS_RATIO gate (forensics.py:47). Local anomaly strength is never evaluated, only global area.

Copy-move of a digit within the same document (the classic '1'→'4' clone): clone detection is disabled outright (forensics.py:458-462), and even enabled its parameters (min 10 matching 16px grid-aligned blocks, >2MP images skipped) could not detect a one-digit clone on a real scan.

Whole-image re-save laundering: attacker edits the scan, then re-exports the ENTIRE image at uniform quality (or screenshots their own edit). ELA differences become uniform, the relative mean+3σ threshold adapts, and nothing flags — the dynamic threshold guarantees ~constant tail mass regardless of tampering.

Format-switch laundering: converting the edited image to PNG/Flate before embedding removes all JPEG history; the module runs meaningless ELA anyway (no ext check at forensics.py:354-365) and reports clean with normal confidence.

Vector overlay attack: drawing a white rectangle + new text with PDF operators OVER the original scanned image (what many PDF editors actually do). The embedded image is byte-identical so ELA sees nothing; the promised 'image placed over text' check was never implemented; the paste-noise check only fires if the overlay happens to sit on a regex-matched amount region and survives the text-edge-dominated variance test.

Edits to anything other than currency amounts: dates, IBAN, SIREN/SIRET, names, addresses, reference numbers are outside AMOUNT_PATTERN (images.py:456-460), so the paste-noise check never even looks at them; amounts without two decimals ('1 000 €') are also invisible.

Phone screenshots: none of the 10 SCREEN_RESOLUTIONS are phone-shaped (1170x2532, 1080x2400, 1284x2778...), and any cropped or resized screenshot defeats the exact-dimension match entirely — yet phone screenshots are the dominant modern screenshot form.

Pasted region containing typed text: the noise-variance test expects the pasted area to be QUIETER than its surroundings, but typed replacement text adds edge energy, raising region variance above the /4 threshold → systematically missed (the most common paste actually includes new text).

Fake text layer over an image-only scan: adding invisible OCR-style text (>200 chars/page) suppresses both IMAGE_ONLY and MOSTLY_IMAGE flags (images.py:408-442) while also feeding attacker-chosen text to the content module; similarly, if TrustyFile's own OCR fallback fills text_by_page first, genuine image-only scans stop flagging.

Small tampered images: anything under 200x200 px (stamps, signature images, small pasted logos) is excluded from all forensics (forensics.py:39-40, 360-361), and images under 10px regions are skipped in paste detection.

Bilevel/CCITT fax-style scans (very common for French attestations): converted to PNG on extraction, ELA meaningless, noise layer near-binary — tampering in this whole document class passes both modules.

Noise-matched paste: an attacker who adds synthetic noise (or uses content-aware fill) to the pasted rectangle defeats the variance-ratio test; no higher-order statistic (JPEG 8x8 grid phase, noise spectrum, CFA pattern) is checked.
improvement_ideas: Compute true placed DPI via page.get_image_rects(xref) (pixels / placed-rect-inches) and dedup images by xref; this simultaneously fixes check_resolution_consistency, makes 'full-page image' mean actual page coverage, and stops per-page double counting.

Gate ELA on base_image['ext'] in ('jpeg','jpg'); skip SMasks; do ELA math in float without cv2.multiply saturation; estimate the original quality from the JPEG quantization tables (works fully locally) and re-compress at that estimated quality — this is standard ELA practice and dramatically improves signal.

Replace the global 3%/5% ELA area gate with local statistics: slide a window (or use the text-block map from find_amount_regions) and flag windows whose ELA energy is an outlier vs the image's own distribution. This is what makes a 0.1%-area amount edit detectable while a uniformly re-saved image stays clean.

Rebuild clone detection as overlapping-block or keypoint (ORB) copy-move with offset-vector clustering/RANSAC: genuine copy-move produces many matches sharing ONE consistent offset vector, while table structure produces periodic offsets — this solves the exact false-positive problem that got the feature disabled, and lift the 2MP cap by downscale-then-verify.

Fix the paste-noise physics: mask out text strokes (binarize and dilate) before measuring variance so you compare BACKGROUND noise only; exclude the region from its own neighborhood window; and add a JPEG-blocking-grid phase check (pasted content is rarely aligned to the host image's 8x8 DCT grid) as an independent, noise-robust paste signal.

Broaden the sensitive-region finder beyond AMOUNT_PATTERN: dates, IBAN/BIC, SIREN/SIRET, reference numbers, and totals keywords ('Total', 'TTC', 'Net à payer'); use span-level bboxes instead of whole block bboxes so the analyzed region tightly bounds the value.

Implement the promised occlusion check: use page.get_drawings() and image rects to detect opaque rectangles/images drawn over existing text or over the scanned image in z-order — this directly catches the white-box overlay attack that currently bypasses everything, and it is cheap and local.

Distinguish text-layer provenance: record whether text came from a real text layer or the OCR fallback, and have check_image_only_pdf use the pre-OCR count; treat 'image-only scan' as a document-class signal (route to scan-specific checks, cap stacked scan penalties) rather than letting IMAGE_ONLY + HEAVY_COMPRESSION + ELA pile up on honest scans — this is the single biggest false-positive reducer.

Fix compression heuristics: bytes-per-pixel adjusted for actual channel count and bpc, or better, decode the JPEG quantization tables to estimate save quality and count of re-saves (double-quantization detection is also a strong tamper signal and fully local).

Modernize screenshot detection: add phone/tablet resolutions, use aspect-ratio families plus UI-chrome cues (status bar strip, uniform top band) instead of exact dimensions, and downgrade severity to medium — screenshots are a provenance signal, not proof of fraud (project goal: minimize false positives).

Error handling and honesty: try/finally around doc.close(); when a check throws, lower the module's confidence and attach an 'analysis incomplete' note instead of silently reporting clean; delete dead code (images.py:321-326 TODO loop, unused suspicious_images) or move disabled clone code behind an explicit experimental flag.

Architecture: extract images once (in pdf_extractor) and pass decoded arrays + placed rects + ext to both Module F and Module H; render each page once and share the pixmap — removes 2 of 3 redundant PDF opens and roughly halves this area's runtime.

Add positive trust signals from this area (project goal 2): e.g., 'digital PDF with vector graphics and coherent single-pass JPEG images', 'scan with uniform noise statistics across all sensitive regions' — small confidence bonuses that help confirm legitimate files instead of only penalizing.
Centralize SEVERITY_POINTS/score deltas in scoring.py and import them, removing the duplicated tables in images.py:662-667 and forensics.py:464-470.
